A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–H are readable and support comparison. v2 additionally includes a NeurIPS checklist.

before.justification: v1 reports original DP-SGD classification experiments on SST-2 and CIFAR-10, numerical bound comparisons, and query-answering simulations in Section 4 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and simulations, including classification accuracies and numerical privacy-risk comparisons.

M1.justification: Appendix D adds a proposed privacy-profile-based calculation of a Bayes-error bound through Proposition D.1, supplementing the existing minimization over the trade-off curve. This is a limited extension of the risk-calculation approach; the unified framework and experimental noise-calibration workflows remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate SST-2, CIFAR-10, the US 2020 Census release, Gaussian and Laplace mechanisms, binary attribute inference, and composed statistical queries. v2's medical-data and document-privacy examples are explanatory scenarios, not additional evaluations.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain Cohen and Nissim's PSO bound, Balle et al.'s RDP/zCDP bounds, Guo et al.'s Fano-based analytical and Monte Carlo bounds, and the standard smartnoise composition analysis. Expanded discussion of Hayes et al. does not add an evaluated comparator.

E3.justification: Section 4 and Appendices D and G retain the same mechanisms, adjacency relations, noise settings, sample sizes, and evaluation metrics. The GPT-2/LoRA and CIFAR-10 hyperparameter tables are unchanged, including batch sizes, epochs, clipping norms, and noise grids.

E4.justification: The Bernoulli-prior comparison, statistical-query case study, CIFAR-10 case study, and supplementary analyses across baselines, dataset sizes, and mechanisms are retained. The additional limitations and threat-model examples in v2 do not introduce new empirical analyses.

E5.justification: Appendix D still specifies 10,000 Monte Carlo samples, ten repetitions, and visually negligible error bars. No uncertainty estimates, seed information, run counts, or statistical procedures change. The new checklist explains the absence of significance reporting for the main theoretical calculations.

E6.justification: The experimental curves and reported findings are retained, including SST-2 accuracy of 52% versus 70% at risk 0.15, CIFAR-10 accuracy of 65% versus 68% at risk 0.25, and the Census risk values. v2's abstract restates the existing SST-2 result rather than reporting a new gain.

T1.justification: v2 adds Proposition D.1 relating Bayes error to the privacy profile and broadens SPSO weights from [0, 1/k] to [0, 1]. It corrects Appendix A's false-positive/false-negative definitions and restricts Lemma C.1's random variable to [0, 1]. However, the revised Lemma 2.1 proof introduces an unsupported inequality in Eq. (27): f(alpha_phi) <= f(alpha) despite alpha_phi <= alpha and non-increasing f.

C1.justification: v2 adds code release as an explicit introductory contribution and qualifies protection by the chosen privacy unit in the conclusion. The central claims of unified, tunable bounds, approximately 20% less noise, and improved classification utility remain unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly distinguishes document-level from individual-level protection, develops marketer/journalist examples for choosing baseline risk, and acknowledges that group-privacy-based bounds can become vacuous with dataset size. It also adds a general-tightness conjecture and discussion of relaxed adversaries as future work.

D1.justification: v2 adds a direct riskcal code-release link and states in the checklist that supplementary code includes reproduction instructions. v1 only identified riskcal as software used. The software list drops SciPy, while hardware, runtime, and hyperparameter disclosures remain unchanged. The PDFs do not establish an underlying implementation change.

R1.justification: Section 5 now explicitly states that the paper subsumes Kaissis et al.'s 2023 workshop paper and explains its relationship to Hayes et al.'s Monte Carlo approach. Appendix B expands attack-aware calibration positioning. Citations are added on Bayes error, realistic adversaries, and privacy units, while several background citations are removed.

P1.justification: v2 makes targeted explanatory rewrites and terminology corrections while retaining the main narrative. Former Appendix B material moves into A.2–A.3, some related-work discussion moves into a repurposed Appendix B, and a NeurIPS checklist is appended. Theorem and lemma labels and cross-references are revised.

P2.justification: The NeurIPS template substantially changes presentation throughout: a redesigned title and author block, narrower text columns, revised typography, and rescaled figures and tables. Figure 6 is restyled, Figure 7's risk-axis wording changes, and Table 1 moves ahead of Figure 8. The underlying displayed comparisons are retained.

improvement.justification: Clearer privacy-unit and baseline qualifications, more explicit attribution to prior work, and code-access information modestly improve interpretability and reproducibility while preserving the empirical evidence. These gains are tempered by the unsupported monotonicity step introduced in Appendix C, Eq. (27); the theoretical editing is therefore not uniformly an improvement.
